header: Where the words of a quote are on a PDF page (pure, no pdf.js in it, so it can be tested): the viewer (PdfPageView.tsx) hands over the page's text pieces with their places, and gets back the rectangles to paint behind the quoted words. A manual's text layer cuts a sentence into pieces (a word, half a line, a line) and breaks lines anywhere, so I put both the page and the quote in one plain form first (lower case, straight quotes, no spaces at all: a raised "th" of "26th" is a piece of its own, and where a space falls between two pieces is not reliable), look for the quote in the page's text as a whole, and each piece it touches gives a rectangle for the part of it that the quote covers (by the width of the text, measured by the caller, or by character count). I guess nothing: if the words are not on the page the answer is no rectangles, and the viewer says so.

symbols.name: readingOrder
symbols.sig: export function readingOrder(pieces: readonly Piece[]): Piece[]
doc: The pieces of a page in the order a reader reads them, column by column, when the page has columns: a book page set in two columns is cut by pdf.js line by line across both columns, so a sentence that runs from one line to the next is broken by a line of the other column. I find the columns from the left edges of the long pieces (the lines of a column start at one place; four or more lines starting together make a column); each piece goes to the nearest column edge at or before it, and I read each column from its top to its bottom. A page without two such columns comes back as it was.

symbols.sig: export function findQuote(pieces: readonly Piece[], quote: string, measure: (text: string) => number = (t) => t.length): Rect[]
doc: Gives the rectangles behind every place the quote is written on the page (empty when it is not there): I try the order the pieces came in first and, if it is not found so, reading order (columns)

behaviours: plain: lower case, no spaces, straight quotes and hyphens
a sentence cut into pieces, with a raised 'th' of its own, is found and covers every piece from the first to the last
a sentence over two lines gives a rectangle on each line and none on the next line
curly quotes and a different hyphen on the page still match the straight ones in the quote
words that are not on the page give no rectangle (nothing is guessed)
a quote written twice on the page is marked in both places
inside one piece only the part the quote covers is marked, in proportion to the characters (D..G of ten is 30 to 70 per cent of its width)
a page in two columns, cut by pdf.js line by line ACROSS the columns, still finds a sentence that runs down one column (read column by column), and marks only that column's lines
a stray one-letter piece between two lines (a decorative 'I' kept by the text layer) does not stop the sentence being found
when the caller measures widths the rectangle follows them: 'WWW' after 'iii ' (4 narrow, 9 wide of 13) starts 4/13 of the way and is 9/13 wide
the matrix product places a page point: (50,60) under a scale of 2 that flips the page on a height of 800 is (100, 680)
a pdf.js text item becomes a piece: its left edge, its top (baseline minus the font height) and its width at the page's scale
